en: (Tatkramapaṭala 75) (Pariśiṣṭa Saṃvat 2042) (The Tattvaśodhana-nāma)
(Leaf 6) (Subject:

Tantra) Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa! [I bow] to the triad of gurus beginning with Śrīnātha, to Gaṇapati, to the three seats, to Bhairava, to the lineage of Siddhas, to the triad of Baṭukas, to the pair of feet, to the sequence of splendor, and to the Śāmbhava [tradition].

One should describe the mandala of the Guru, which consists of eight Vīreśas, four groups of sixty-four, nine [Vīras], and five Vīrāvalīs, together with the King of Mantras, the Śrīman Mālinī. (1) Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ!

Having been churned in the midst of the ocean, in the nectar-sea, the best of oceans, the Goddess Surā was born from the mantra, assuming the form of a maiden. (2) The Goddess has eighteen arms, her eyes rolling from intoxication;

she is three-eyed, her limbs are long and slender, and she resembles the fire of cosmic destruction (Kālāgni). (3) Standing within the mandala itself, she is adorned with nectar produced from the foam.

She whose complexion is yellowish-red, black, and pale white; she who possesses the luster of molten gold, adorned with a pure radiance; she whose color is like cow’s urine or milk, and who is auspiciously endowed with every other hue—she who constantly terrifies the Asuras and bestows fearlessness upon the gods; she who is Umā, the goddess, he who is Mada, the Great Lord Maheśvara; he who is Yoga, he becomes Brahmā; he who is Āhlāda, he is Janārdana; he who is established as Svāda, he is Soma; and he who is in the foam is called Anala. In the shadow is Manmatha.

The excellent Bhairava Devanālāmbu is [the essence]; all the oceans are said to reside within this vessel, which is known as the Gaṅgā of substances. (8) By means of this thread of the vessel, the purification of the substance is accomplished;
you are the very nature of substance, existing in the form of power (*śakti*), fashioned by Brahmā in the beginning. (9) Having cast away that which is impure, the practitioner shall bestow success.

Having thus consecrated it and filled the jar, one should fill the sacred water (*tīrtha*) therein from the center of the vessel: "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā... O Kuru... (10) "This is my Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudri, and Soma..."

[The hymns] *catāparūṣṭyā*, *asiknyāmarudvṛdhe*, *vitastayārjīkīye*, and *śṛṇuyā suṣomayā* [are recited]. (11) Where the white and black rivers meet, there they bathe and fly up to heaven. In this very way, the wise release their bodies and thereby partake in immortality. (12) One should worship the water-pot (*kalaśa*) on the left. Having established the common conch (*śaṅkha*) on the right, one should sprinkle oneself and the ritual implements with the water from those two vessels. With that same water, one should draw a triangle in the southern part of the conch.

Having constructed a mandala consisting of a square with nine enclosures and a hexagon, one should worship the center with the root mantra (*mūla*). Then, having worshipped the three-syllable Vidyā within the triangle, one should worship the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) in the six corners. Having established the tripod (*tripādikā*) with the mantra: *Aiṃ agnimaṇḍalāya daśakalātmane arghyapātrādhārāya namaḥ*, one should then recite this seed-mantra (*bīja*) three times for each name in clockwise order, starting from the front: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ dhūmrārciṣe oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ.* *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ uṣmāyai śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ.* (2) *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālinyai śrīṃ hrīṃ...*

Oṃ namaḥ. (3) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jvālinyai śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ. (4) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ visphuliṅginyai śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ. (5) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ suśriyai. (6) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ surūpāyai. (7) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kapilāyai. (8) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ havyavāhāyai. (9) Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kavyavāhāyai. (10) Having thus worshipped the one whose nature consists of these ten digits (*kalā*s), one should place the vessel with: "Klīṃ, obeisance to the vessel for the *arghya* offering, which is the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*) consisting of twelve digits. Within that [vessel]: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ...

*Tapinyai śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ*. Thus for all [subsequent names]. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ tāpinyai (0)*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ dhūmrāyai (0)*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ viśvāyai (0)*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ bodhinyai (0)*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ dhāriṇyai (0)*. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kṣamāyai (0)*. Having thus worshipped, [one should worship] in the center thereof: *Sauḥ somamaṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśakalātmane arghyāmṛtāya (0)*.

Having thus filled the first [corner], in the middle of the first [corner]: (3) *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ aṃ amṛtāyai śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ*. Thus for all [corners]. *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ āṃ mānasyai śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ* (3).

*Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ iṃ pūṣāyai śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ* (3). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ īṃ tuṣṭyai* (0). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ uṃ puṣṭyai* (0). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ ūṃ ratyai* (0). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ ṛṃ dhṛtyai* (0). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ ṝ śaśinyai* (0). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ ḷ candrikāyai* (0). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ ḹ kāntyai* (0). *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ*...

Oṃ aiṃ utsnāyai (0) oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ aiṃ śrīyai (0) oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ oṃ prītyai (0) oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ auṃ aṅgadāyai (0) oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ aṃ pūrṇāyai (0) oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ aḥ pūrṇāmṛtāyai (0). Then, having placed the second [syllable] with the Kāmarāja mantra: oṃ amṛtāyai (0) oṃ mānadāyai (0) oṃ puṣṭyai (0) oṃ tuṣṭyai (0) oṃ priyāyai (0) oṃ varadāyai (0) oṃ manojñāyai (0) oṃ divyāmṛtasomāyai namaḥ.

Now, the mantra for the water-pot (*kalaśa*): "The winds blow sweetly for the one who follows the cosmic order (*ṛta*). O seekers of the prize, come to us in every contest for wealth; O wise ones, knowers of the eternal truth, drink of this honeyed mead and rejoice! Quench your thirst by the paths traveled by the gods. Having performed the *akathādi-pakti* [ritual] starting from the mouth and proceeding clockwise a hundred thousand times, and having likewise written and meditated upon the middle syllable accompanied by the three seed-syllables of the Virgin (*kumārī*), one should worship it with the mantra "Haṃsaḥ" (the Swan). Thus it is said.
Now, the purification of substances: Next, one should recite the *Surā-gāyatrī* twenty-eight times: *Oṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ surādevīṃ vidmahe amṛtodravīṃ dhīmahi tanno raktākṣi pracodayāt*.

Now, the removal of curses (*śāpavimocana*): *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ śrāvaya 2 amṛtaṃ drāvaya 2 amṛtaṃ plāvaya 2 mama pātre amṛtaṃ pūraya 2 candramaṇḍalanivāsini śukraśāpaṃ mocaya 2 [the substance]*.

Purify [it]! Svāhā! Oṃ Krom! Salutation to the Lord of the Daityas, the Lord of Śukra! Having consecrated [the wine] thus seven times, one should dispel any defect by scattering flowers and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) into the center of the vessel with this mantra: "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the touch of the defect of all women, Huṃ Phaṭ! Salutation! Then, one should cause the nectar to flow by reciting this mantra: "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Blūṃ Hsau Jūṃ Saḥ! O Nectar! O Source of Nectar! O Mistress of Nectar! O Rainer of Nectar! Cause the nectar to flow! Svāhā! Thus, one should cause the wine to flow, [removing] the curses of Śukra and the others.

*Unmocaya svāhā*. Again, the Gāyatrī: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ sudhādevyai vidmahe, klīṃ kāmeśvaryai dhīmahi, sauḥ tannaḥ tuṣṭiḥ pracodayāt*. Having consecrated [the substance] thus, protect it with the Astra-mantra, veil it with the Kavaca-mantra, and transform it into nectar using the Amṛta-bīja. Again, consecrate it seven times with: *Oṃ kroṃ daityanāthāya śukranāthāya namaḥ*. Then, display the Dhenu and Yoni mudrās, cover it with the Matsya mudrā, and [recite]: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ brāṃ brīṃ brūṃ*.

Having consecrated [the nectar] twelve times with: *braiṃ brauṃ braḥ brahmaśāpavimocakāyai sudhādevyai svāhā*, and having consecrated it ten times with: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ kṛṣṇaśāpavimocakāyai sudhādevyai svāhā*, and having consecrated it twelve times with: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ saiṃ sauṃ saḥ śukraśāpavimocakāyai sudhādevyai svāhā*—in this very manner, one should [offer] the Supreme Brahman, which consists of the gross and the subtle, the eternal, and the sin of Brahmin-slaughter born from the hair (*kaca*).

By this very [mantra], I pacify it: "O Goddess, born from the solar disc, born from the abode of Varuṇa, may the seed-syllable *Amā* be released by me from the curse of Śukra. If the *praṇava* is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess, may my sin of killing a Brahmin (*brahmahatyā*) be dispelled. *Oṃ namo bhagavati vāruṇi jalamūrte śukrādiśāpavimocani idaṃ dravyaṃ pavitraṃ kuru amṛtaṃ kuru svāhā*. *Aiṃ* to the curse of Śukra, *klīṃ* to the unfailing weapon, *sauḥ* release!"

"Yaḥ svāhā! O You who are the essence of substance, whose form is power, and who are eternally dear to the three worlds; having cast away all that is impure, [be present] for the sake of the practitioner’s desired accomplishment. Having meditated thus, one should offer the *pathika-bali* with this mantra: "Oṃ namo bhagavati vāruṇi jalamūrte grāmeśvari pathikadevatāyai, liberate me from all defects, liberate me from all curses, svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the deities of the travelers (*pathikadevatābhyaḥ*). With this mantra, one should offer water mixed with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and saffron.

Having whirled [the vessel] above all the substances, one should cast [the water] toward the north with "Vauṣaṭ. Having sprinkled [them] with the root mantra, consecrated them with the Gāyatrī, and consecrated them eight times with the root-vidyā, one should offer sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, flowers, incense, and lamps. Regarding that, having sprinkled all the materials to be worshipped with the *vitpuṅbhi* [mantra] and having perceived them all as being composed of Brahman (*brahmamaya*), one should worship them. This is the purification of their presiding deity; may there be auspiciousness. Having uttered the root mantra "Oṃ Hrīṃ," [one says]: "O Śrī Sviṣṭadevatā, come (2)! Descend into the seat (2)!"

Having invoked [the deity] with the mantra, "Come! Be present before me!"—then follows the preparation of the vessels (*pātrāsādhana*). First, one should prepare the jar (*kuṃbha*), the conch (*śaṅkha*), the *Śrīpātra*, the *Śaktipātra*, the *Balipātra*, the *Baṭukapātra*, and the *Gurupātra* (which is remembered as the vessel of nectar). Then, to the north of the conch, having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square, one should worship with: "Obeisance to the support of the vessel for the goddess consisting of ten kalās of the fire-mandala. For these are the ten kalās of fire, which bestow the fruit of the tenfold dharma.

Accompanied by the *tobhas*, one should always perform the protection of the Āditya [mantra]: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaplāvini pātre amṛtaṃ pūraya* (2) *caṃdramaṇḍalanivāsini śukraśāpaṃ muñca* (2) *dravyaṃ pavitrīkuru* (2) *svāhā*. One should recite this seven times.
Now follows the purification of the principles (*tattva-śodhana*). *Oṃ aiṃ prakṛti-ahaṃkāra-buddhi-manas-śrotra-tvak-cakṣus-jihvā-ghrāṇa-vāk-pāṇi-pāda-pāyu-upastha-* [and so forth].

O Self of sound, touch, form, taste, smell, ether, air, fire, water, and earth; O Aṃ, Aṃ, and so forth, for fifteen times; O Self of the principle of the Self; O Self of the universal Person; O Self of the universal Person; O Self accompanied by Sarasvatī and Hiraṇyagarbha; O Self accompanied by Sarasvatī and Hiraṇyagarbha—for the sake of purifying the subtle lotus, I purify the gross body in the foundation (ādhāra) by means of the principle of the Self, [unto] my chosen deity.

*Laṃ*, this great supreme nectar produced from the vessel of *idaṃtā* (this-ness), I offer into the fire of supreme, disease-free consciousness, attaining the state of Śiva: *Aiṃ ātmatattvaṃ śodhayāmi namaḥ svāhā*. (1) *Klīṃ*, [I offer] unto the self consisting of Māyā, Kalā, Vidyā, Rāga, Kāla, Niyati, and Puruṣa. (25) Twenty-five times, [I offer] unto the Vidyātattva, unto the self of the Vidyātattva, unto the Taijasa Puruṣa, and unto the self of the Taijasa Puruṣa, together with Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.

For the sake of purifying the impurities of the manifold karmic body, I purify the subtle body within the heart by means of the *vidyā-tattva*. In the root-mantra: *Aṃ*, within that certain ground of the expansion of the rays of the wondrous light of consciousness—the fire that is the adversary to the darkness of delusion, which is internal, continuous, stainless, and all-pervading—I sacrifice everything from the earth (*vasudhā*) up to the state of *Śivā*. *Klīṃ*, I purify the *vidyā-tattva*; *namaḥ svāhā*. *Sauḥ*, [I purify] Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, and Śuddhavidyā.

This [offering], which is of the nature of the Self of awakened knowledge (*vidyātman*), is for the sake of the ten-fold Śiva-principle; to the Self who is the Śiva-principle, to the Wise Being (*prājñapuruṣa*), to the Self who is the Wise Being, accompanied by Vidyā-Śaṅkara, to the Self accompanied by Vidyā-Śaṅkara—for the purpose of purifying this single lotus, I purify the portion of the causal body by means of the Śiva-principle.
May the Mothers be satisfied at the root, as well as all the Bhairavas together with the Vināyakas, the Kṣetrapālas, and the Yoginīs residing within my body. *Sauḥ*.

I purify the Śivatattva; *namaḥ svāhā*. *Aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, [to] Prakṛti, Ahaṃkāra, Buddhi, Manas, Śrotra, Tvak, Cakṣus, Jihvā, Ghrāṇa, Vāk, Pāṇi, Pāda, Pāyu, Upastha, Śabda, Sparśa, Rūpa, Rasa, Gandha, Ākāśa, Vāyu, Agni, Salila, Bhūmi, Māyā, Kalā, Vidya, Rāga, Kāla, Niyati, Puruṣa, Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, Śuddhavidyā, and Ātman—*aṃ āṃ*, and so forth.

To the one whose form ends with the letter *ḍakāra*, to the essence of all principles (*sarvatattva*), to the self of all principles, to the Puruṣas Viśva, Taijasa, and Prājña, to the self of the Puruṣas Viśva, Taijasa, and Prājña,

to the one accompanied by Sarasvatī, Hiraṇyagarbha, Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa, Vidyā, and Śaṅkara, to the self accompanied by Sarasvatī, Hiraṇyagarbha, Lakṣmī, Nārāyaṇa, Vidyā, and Śaṅkara— for the sake of purifying the lotus of the *āṇava*, *kārmika*, and *māyika* [impurities], [to the self] gross and subtle...

I purify the body of causes and great causes through the oneness of the individual soul (jīva) and the Supreme Self (paramātman) as the reality of all things. With the mind as the ladle, I offer the oblation of dharma and adharma into the blazing fire of the Self, which resides in the *mūlādhāra*, while constantly flowing through the *suṣumṇā* and consuming the functions of the senses. *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ*, I purify [this] as the reality of all things; *namaḥ svāhā*. Having placed the vessel upon the *ādhāra*, from the *mūlādhāra* up to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*)...
Having meditated upon that Kuṇḍalinī in her true form, one should display the mudrās according to one's ability, recite [the mantra] with the root rosary, and offer it.

Thus ends the purification of the principles (tattva-śodhana). [Thus the purification of the principles is complete. In the year 1727, on the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada, on Thursday, for the sake of both self and others, by Vāstavya Mallāragaḍe. Now begins the section on Dīpanātha. Oṃ, salutations to the venerable Gurus. Ya...
The practitioner, residing in that village, having installed [the image] there for the sake of the deity [Name], [Name]-śarman, and [Name]-dīpanātha;
then—
